reason: I want to follow how the kidney separates blood contents before recovering useful substances. The filter picture shows small substances can pass through its gaps.
expectation: I expect water and other small substances to enter the filter space while blood cells and large proteins stay in the blood; I’m unsure exactly what happens next.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would start the route to the bladder, but I want to explore filtering first.

effect: The filter lets useful glucose, salts and water through along with wastes, so I want to follow their recovery next.
reaction: It was interesting that the filter doesn't just separate out waste.
reason: The recovery tube's picture shows useful substances moving back toward the blood, continuing the filtering route.
expectation: I expect glucose, some salts and much water to return to the blood, leaving some fluid and waste in the tube.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would build the bladder route, but I want to finish following recovery first.

effect: Recovery returns useful substances and much water to the blood, leaving waste-containing fluid to collect.
reaction: It makes more sense why filtering and recovery are both needed.
reason: The ureters connect the kidneys toward the bladder, so they start the drainage route.
expectation: I expect the ureters to attach to the kidney pair, with the bladder still to be added.

alternatives.reason: The bladder is also needed, but I want to connect the tubes from the kidneys first.

effect: The ureters now lead down from the kidneys, leaving the bladder to complete the route.
reason: Adding the bladder is the only offered combination and should complete the drainage route.
expectation: I expect the bladder to attach to the ureters so urine can collect there.

effect: The ureters now connect the kidneys to the bladder, providing a continuous drainage route.
reaction: The completed route was clear and as expected.
reason: The only offered combination follows the remaining fluid into the completed drainage route.
expectation: I expect the waste-containing fluid to travel as urine through the ureters and collect in the bladder.

effect: The remaining fluid reached the bladder as urine, completing the route while blood continued through separate vessels.
reaction: The ending was clear, though it was what I expected.

mostWorthwhile.text: Filtering and then recovering useful substances was most worthwhile: it showed why the kidney cannot simply filter out waste.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the bladder was straightforward but less engaging; it was the only offered combination at that point.

surprise.text: I was surprised that useful glucose and water pass through the filter along with waste.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the pictures and goals explained the route, although the last two choices were the only offered combinations.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see another body system, though the final connections were predictable and the compatible-pair menu did much of the guiding.
